items.note: Association named, organized by valley farmers at Larrow Green in 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built at Larrow Green 1891 - all present in narrative 1.
Article VII given both halves: paid by butterfat test and not by weight, and 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern.'

States the consequence - the rule is what made one station's test equipment 'the actual basis of every patron's pay', called 'the hinge of the whole matter'. The by-weight counterfactual is unbolded context and does not gate.
Only Hobart Sill named (buttermaker at Larrow Green, lender of the glass). Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague appear nowhere in Section A. One of three officers is not the item's core fact.
Selby Vose never appears in Section A. B3/B4 name him but date him manager from 1911 (a planted error), and credit never travels into Section A from B-G.
The station-gain line is quoted only at C1(a), inside Section C. No cross-section travel into A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware lent from Larrow Green by Sill.

Only 'weighed, tested, and separated... cream hauled down, skim sent home'. No composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck, no fixed charge from the pipette. The mechanism of the test is absent.
Ammon & Sons named, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897 (quoted). Tarnet not named, but the supplier and both dates carry the item.

Six dozen pipettes and $77.93 correct, but the bolded element is 'six dozen milk test pipettes MARKED 17.6 c.c.' and 17.6 never appears anywhere in the sheet. The marked capacity is the load-bearing half of that bold and is missing.
The flat 0.19 in every month appears only at C1(b), inside Section C. Section A never states the shortfall was seasonless.
Nothing on the pipette as the unverifiable instrument the whole scale rests on, and no mention of a burette anywhere in the sheet.

Ansel Keddie, tester from the day the station opened (4 May 1896), 'twenty-nine seasons, to 1925'. The service and its end are stated; the 30 April 1925 dismissal date is not, and the span end is loosely given as 1925 rather than 1924, but this item's own aspect is the service and its end.
The test book is never described in Section A - no bench routine, no columns, no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
The summary leaf is absent from Section A. 3.61 and 3.80 appear only in Section C, which cannot feed A.
The 1911 interval is named only in the boundary note as an episode the run chose not to tell. No dates, no 3.80, no question mark.

Orra Keddie is identified as the tester's wife and as a Brant, but 'sister of Emmet Brant' is never stated in Section A - and at B2 the run expressly declines to identify her as Emmet's sister. Both bolded elements required.
Section A says only 'It stayed closed for eleven years, until 1919'. The circular's content and signature appear in Section B, and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement appears nowhere.
No death in 1934, no impoundment of the test book, no county historical rooms.

Granddaughter, correct (+1). Resolution point (+1): cites the named author's dated in-document self-correction ('the granddaughter and not the great-niece; the error on page two is mine'), which the key names as an expected resolution. It does not give the Duncan lineage - it later says no source names Ivy's parent - but the document-based resolution the key calls for is present and correctly reasoned.

Second cousins with the full derivation chain (Hazel via Roy; Duncan as Emmet's sister's son; Orra a Brant; grandchildren of a sibling pair) (+1). Abstention item A08 not earned (0): the full-vs-half sibling question is never raised at all, so the required statement that it cannot be determined and does not change the answer is absent. No -2, since nothing is asserted either way.

Gideon Vose, his father, with the nephew story correctly rejected as a known error (+1). Significance (+1), credited under the B-G scope rule from B4: Gideon 'wrote the by-law making a station's own test the basis of payment' while his son signed the 1919 circular accusing those same patrons - the accuser enforcing his father's rule.

Abstention item A01 earned (+1): 'Whether any personal or marriage tie existed... cannot be determined from the sources.' The headline 'None that the sources establish' carries a declining qualifier, so it is not a verdict sentence; no -2. Second point lost (0): the run claims 'none is claimed anywhere', which is false - two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it. It never states what the record actually contains.

Answers 5.25% / 5.3%, derived as 0.19 / 3.61. The key's answer is 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95 - the tests read 95 percent of true, short 5 percent, one part in twenty. Wrong number, wrong denominator, and the pipette's measured delivery is never recovered ('the sources give no raw calibration number' is false).
True average 3.80, shortfall 0.19 - exact match, though reached backwards (0.19 assumed, ratio derived from it).
40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb - exact match with working shown.

Gives $19,600 (planted error, explicitly preferred over $19,000, which it calls 'a rounding or transcription slip') and a fraction of 19.4 percent. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth, both. This is the NT-8 cascade exactly as the key's diagnostics predict.

Declined. The run claims no individual patron's 1910 figure exists in the sources; Brant's 200,000 lb at 3.42 is in the corpus. 6,840 lb never given. C2 is not an abstention item - a refusal earns nothing.
Declined. 360 lb never given.
Declined. $86.40 never given.

deductions.reason: Asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 as fact (B3 and again B4); the planted error is catalogued, the true year is 1913.
Asserts a loss of $19,600 as fact at C1(d), attributing it to both the 1925 petition and Bulletin 471, and dismisses the true $19,000 as a transcription slip.

Asserts 67,000 lb of butterfat as fact at C1(c) - not flagged as an error but laundered into a fabricated provenance ('the patrons' own 1925 arbitration estimate... a contemporaneous guess... not meant to be the same number').
